rows.citation: Alonso LM, Marder E (2019). Visualization of currents in neural models with similar behavior and different conductance densities. eLife 8:e42722.
rows.model_type: Conductance-based single-compartment bursting neuron models (kinetics following Liu et al. 1998, with calcium dynamics); six degenerate models
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - graded decrements and full deletions of each maximal conductance, studied as biological perturbations, not as seeded faults to evaluate tests.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - constant current injection swept over amplitudes plus conductance perturbations; no battery of distinct protocol types such as ramps, rebound or pulses.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - burst frequency, duty cycle, ISI and voltage distributions, currentscapes; used for visualisation, not thresholded detection.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - a genetic algorithm searches conductances matching target activity; stimuli are not selected or optimised.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - six hand-analysed models; no discovery/held-out split or detection evaluation.
rows.software: none (article reports a Dryad data package, doi:10.5061/dryad.d0779mb, not separately retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Biological precedent that similar baseline activity can hide divergent responses to current injection and conductance changes, motivating multi-stimulus fingerprints. It is a visualisation/degeneracy study; NeuroSem would add model-transformation testing, single-fault mutants with admissibility classification, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.7554/elife.42722 (title, 2 authors, eLife vol 8, e42722, issued 2019-01-31); Europe PMC REST search DOI (PMID 30702427, PMC6395073, abstract); Europe PMC full text https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC6395073/fullTextXML (results sections on current injection, conductance decrements/deletions; methods on GA optimisation; data availability).
rows.found_via: Europe PMC TITLE query (critic query 'similar behavior different conductance densities')

rows.citation: Niederer SA, Kerfoot E, Benson AP, et al. (2011). Verification of cardiac tissue electrophysiology simulators using an N-version benchmark. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences 369(1954):4331-4351.
rows.model_type: Cardiac tissue electrophysiology (ten Tusscher-Panfilov myocyte model in a 3-D cuboid slab), compared across 11 simulation codes
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults; per the article, genuine implementation errors (e.g. unit mistakes) surfaced and were corrected during benchmarking.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - one corner stimulus; per the article, stimulation from multiple sites is left for future benchmarks.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares activation times (0 mV crossing) at points and lines using an L2 norm; no action-potential shape feature set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - highly refined simulations serve as converged reference; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.software: none (benchmark results deposited in the Anatomical Model Database per the article; not separately retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest precedent for refinement-based comparison against a converged reference across implementations (3 spatial x 3 temporal resolutions). NeuroSem differs by targeting single-neuron NeuroML model edits within one simulator, seeding single-fault mutants, using multi-protocol eFEL fingerprints with refinement-derived tolerances, and selecting a compact battery evaluated on held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsta.2011.0139 (title, 21 authors, vol 369 issue 1954 pp 4331-4351, issued 2011-11-13, abstract); Europe PMC REST search DOI (PMID 21969679, PMC3263775); NCBI efetch db=pmc id=3263775 (publisher blocks XML full text); PMC HTML article https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3263775/ read via WebFetch (benchmark definition, resolutions, activation-time comparison).

rows.model_type: Multi-compartment neuron and network simulators (Arbor, NEURON, CoreNEURON); simulator benchmarking and numerical validation on HPC
rows.controlled_mutations: no - validation compares simulator output with reference solutions; docs describe no fault seeding or mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - several validation models (e.g. rallpack1, cable-steadystate, rc-expsyn, rc-exp2syn-spike) each with one or more parameter sets; no per-model stimulus battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - comparex computes absolute/relative errors of NetCDF variables and thresholdx applies pass/fail predicates; no spike-feature extraction documented.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - tests are hand-defined; no protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - fixed validation and benchmark suite; no held-out split.
rows.software: NSuite https://github.com/arbor-sim/nsuite (docs http://nsuite.readthedocs.io; GitHub license field NOASSERTION, LICENSE file is BSD 3-clause-style text, copyright 2019 ETH Zurich and FZ Julich; last push 2024-04-26)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Detects correctness and performance regressions of simulators (including across system changes, for CI) against reference solutions with error thresholds. NeuroSem instead holds the simulator fixed and targets model-file transformations, with single-fault mutants, multi-protocol feature fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances and held-out battery selection.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/arbor-sim/nsuite (description, created 2018-06-11, pushed 2024-04-26, license NOASSERTION); /readme and root/docs/validation directory listings; raw docs/validation.rst and docs/index.rst; raw LICENSE file.

rows.citation: neuronsimulator (2021). nrn-modeldb-ci: NEURON ModelDB CI tools. GitHub repository and PyPI package, https://github.com/neuronsimulator/nrn-modeldb-ci.
rows.model_type: Published NEURON (HOC/NMODL) models fetched from ModelDB, run unchanged across NEURON versions/builds
rows.controlled_mutations: no - varies the NEURON build (e.g. release vs nightly), not the models; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each model runs its own mosinit/driver script or custom run instructions; no systematic stimulus battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - diffs graph output (gout), stdout and run status between NEURON versions, with regex curation of noisy output; no feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - runs all or specified ModelDB NEURON models (nightly and on PRs); no split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest neuroscience execution-stack regression CI: many published models, raw-output diffs between simulator versions (README example report lists 659 models run). NeuroSem targets edits to the model files, probes behaviour beyond each model's default run with a stimulus battery, uses feature-level refinement-calibrated tolerances instead of output diffs, and evaluates mutant detection on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/neuronsimulator/nrn-modeldb-ci (created 2021-11-05, pushed 2026-09-05, BSD-3-Clause); raw README.md (commands getmodels/runmodels/diffreports2html, gout diffs, curate_patterns); PyPI JSON https://pypi.org/pypi/nrn-modeldb-ci/json (version 0.3.0, BSD-3-Clause).

rows.citation: Scott-Brown J, Papachristodoulou A (2016). sbml-diff: A Tool for Visually Comparing SBML Models in Synthetic Biology. ACS Synthetic Biology 6(7):1225-1229.
rows.model_type: SBML biochemical reaction network models (synthetic/systems biology)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares existing model versions; no fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - produces static diagrams; no simulation or stimulation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - structural diagram views of species, reactions, rules and events only.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - tool description; no evaluation split.
rows.software: sbml-diff https://github.com/jamesscottbrown/sbml-diff (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API and abstract)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Represents structural/visual model-version diffing without simulation. NeuroSem addresses behavioural changes that structural comparison cannot reveal, by simulating model versions under multiple stimuli and comparing calibrated electrophysiology features.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1021/acssynbio.6b00273 (title, 2 authors, ACS Synth Biol vol 6 issue 7 pp 1225-1229, issued 2016-12-30, abstract); GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/jamesscottbrown/sbml-diff (BSD-3-Clause). Year follows Crossref issued date (2016); volume/issue are 2017.

rows.citation: Kamali AH, Giannoulatou E, Chen TY, et al. (2015). How to test bioinformatics software? Biophysical Reviews 7(3):343-352.
rows.model_type: General bioinformatics/scientific software (review; examples from systems biology simulators and genomic medicine)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - reviews mutation analysis (fault-injected mutants, mutation score) for judging test effectiveness; reports no new mutation study.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - review of testing methods; no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no electrophysiology or neuron models discussed.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - discusses test case selection (adaptive random testing, diverse metamorphic relations); no stimulus-protocol selection.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background review of testing concepts NeuroSem draws on (N-version, metamorphic, random/adaptive random testing, mutation analysis; SBML simulator comparisons). NeuroSem would contribute a concrete neuron-model instantiation with electrophysiology fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
